newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat ratings improve, disease a concern.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat ratings improve, disease a concern.

text.p: Oklahoma's wheat crop improved slightly but more disease pressure was evident during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop weather report.
"The condition of the 1997 wheat crop has improved from earlier reported freeze damage," the report said. "Disease pressures appear to concern many growers in western Oklahoma."

Wheat was rated 10 percent very poor, 17 poor, 39 fair, 33 good and one excellent. That was a mild improvement over the previous week's rating of 14 percent very poor, 18 poor, 35 fair, 32 good and one excellent.
The state's wheat acreage was 78 percent headed, behind 86 percent in 1996 and 84 for the five-year average.

In major production areas of the Oklahoma Panhandle, corn plantings made significant headway while sorghum plantings remained nearly nonexistent. Corn was 56 percent planted, well behind 97 last year and the 91 percent average.
Soybeans were 32 percent planted, slightly ahead of the five-year average of 22 percent.

Livestock conditions were rated two percent poor, 16 fair, 77 good and five excellent. That marked an improvement over the previous week's ratings of three percent poor, 20 percent fair, 72 percent good and five percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated two percent short, 90 adequate and eight percent surplus.
